definition: Contracts in regulated markets where a regulated utility agrees to buy power from a third-party generator, used to secure a sufficient supply of renewable power.
core_idea: PPAs let a regulated utility lock in renewable supply from third-party generators, functioning as one of the tools (alongside ancillary services and capacity markets) grids use to secure adequate generation resources.
key_points: PPAs are described in the context of regulated markets, where the regulated utility signs directly with third-party generators.
Their stated purpose in this text is specifically to secure renewable power supply.
relationships: Grouped with ancillary services and capacity markets as demand/supply-adequacy tools.
